what_it_is.prose: ThyssenKrupp Marine Systems (TKMS) is a German naval defence OEM headquartered in Kiel, Germany, and one of the world's leading conventional submarine builders. TKMS, formerly HDW (Howaldtswerke-Deutsche Werft), has built over 180 submarines for 14 navies worldwide, including the Type 209 and its successor, the Type 214 — one of the most proven AIP-capable conventional submarine designs in service. TKMS is a leading competitor for India's ₹43,000 crore Project 75I programme to build 6 AIP-equipped submarines, offering the HDW Class 214 design with a proven fuel-cell Air-Independent Propulsion (AIP) system. The Class 214 has been selected by South Korea (KSS-II programme, 9 boats), Greece, Portugal, Turkey, and Israel. For P75I, TKMS has partnered with Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders (MDL) as the Indian build yard. The fuel-cell AIP system on the Class 214 is a mature, operationally proven design that eliminates the noise of diesel generators during submerged operations, extending submerged endurance to ~3 weeks without snorkelling.

faq.question: What is TKMS offering for India's Project 75I?
faq.answer: TKMS is offering the HDW Class 214 conventional submarine with a proven fuel-cell Air-Independent Propulsion (AIP) system for India's Project 75I (6 submarines, ~₹43,000 crore). The Class 214 has been selected by 14 navies globally, with the fuel-cell AIP validated in German and South Korean submarines. For P75I, TKMS has partnered with Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders (MDL) as the Indian build yard.

faq.question: What makes the Class 214 AIP system significant?
faq.answer: The Class 214 uses a proton-exchange membrane (PEM) fuel-cell AIP system that generates electricity from hydrogen and oxygen without combustion, eliminating the noise associated with diesel generators. This allows the submarine to remain submerged for up to ~3 weeks without snorkelling, dramatically reducing the risk of detection. The AIP system has been operationally validated in the German Navy (Type 212A) and South Korean Navy (KSS-II), and is considered the most mature AIP design available for export.

faq.question: How does TKMS compare with Naval Group for P75I?
faq.answer: TKMS and Naval Group are the two leading foreign contenders for P75I. Naval Group's advantage is the operational validation of its Scorpene design through India's 6 Kalvari-class boats. TKMS's advantage is its proven fuel-cell AIP technology (more mature than Naval Group's MESMA steam-turbine AIP) and its track record of exporting to 14 navies. The Indian DRDO-NPOL indigenous design is the third contender. Contract award is expected in 2026.
